rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA adds back THREE new items not present in Q1 2025: (i) pension buy-out settlement loss of $16.6M (U.K. defined-benefit plan); (ii) servicing liability, fees and amortization $11.2M; (iii) non-operating items related to the Greystone JV $12.9M. rfm_tuples.interpretation: The +16% Adjusted EBITDA growth headline is real ONLY if you accept three new add-backs as truly non-recurring. The pension buy-out IS one-time. Strip those two and 'true' adjusted EBITDA growth is roughly $111.3M - $12.9M - $11.2M = $87.2M, BELOW the $96.2M prior year — a 9% DECLINE not a 16% increase. Pattern matches 'aggressive non-GAAP design' rather than fraud, but the narrative is contestable.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Three non-GAAP measures DROPPED Q1 2026: (1) Service line fee revenue — this was the comparable revenue line that excluded gross contract reimbursables (lower-margin pass-throughs); dropping it makes top-line growth look MORE robust (Q1 2026 +11% on total revenue vs +9% on fee revenue prior basis); (2) Adjusted EBITDA margin — dropped; CWK was tracking 9.3% margin in FY25 (up 46bps YoY); removing this denominator means investors can no longer easily compute margin trajectory; (3) Segment operating expenses / Fee-based operating expenses — dropped; these were the cleanest cost-side comparables. New segment reporting is on TOTAL revenue and adds 'Gross contract costs' / 'Direct employment costs' / etc. as the cost decomposition — i.e., MORE line items, LESS comparability. On 2026-04-08, company posted RECAST historical financials to IR website (without an 8-K Item 2.02 announcement) — accommodative gesture but the recast was on the new framework. 'Other segment items' add-back in Q1 2026 includes 'certain non-GAAP adjustments for unusual, non-recurring or non-operating items used to calculate Adjusted EBITDA' — i.e., the segment-level Adjusted EBITDA add-back layer is now MORE judgmental.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch. The simultaneous (a) dropping of Service Line Fee Revenue, (b) dropping of Adjusted EBITDA Margin, and (c) dropping of Segment Operating Expenses — all in Q1 2026, the SAME quarter where GAAP swung to a -$12.6M loss — is classic 'disclosure gating' that eliminates the cleanest YoY comparable metrics precisely as the metrics turn against the issuer. Recast files were posted to IR website but the simultaneity is the tell. Honesty-alpha framing: the disclosures remain honest in the sense that GAAP statements are still complete, but management has REDUCED the ease of investor comparability at the moment that ease most matters. Not fraud, but a quiet erosion of disclosure discipline.

summary: CWK is a -25.1% drawdown global real estate services name where the Form-4 tape REJECTS any management-conviction narrative: in 12 months across 35 Form 4 filings / 51 transactions, ZERO open-market purchases (code P) vs $379K of code-S sales. CEO Michelle MacKay, CFO Neil Johnston, COO Andrew McDonald, EVP Robinson, GC Perkins, CAO Sayed — ALL have personal-capital deployment of $0 into the drawdown; their only transactions are code-F tax-withholding around RSU vesting (~$6.3M sold to cover taxes on previously-granted equity at $0 strike). EVP Robinson sold 10,000 sh @ $13.50 on 2026-03-03 (12 days post 10-K) and AGAIN 10,000 sh @ $13.52 on 2026-05-12 (5 days post Q1 earnings, 13 days pre-cutoff) — scaling out of weakness. Company-level discretionary buyback: $0 disclosed; capital allocation skewed entirely to debt paydown (3 Term Loan repricings, $300M optional prepayment, $100M partial redemption of 2028 Notes on 5/15). Operational pain centered on Greystone JV: $177M Q4 2025 OTH impairment + $24.9M CWK-share loan-loss provision + Q3 2025 expansion of Fannie Mae loss-share list to 65 loans + Freddie Mac indemnity on 42 brokered loans — multi-year tail, not 'one-time' as framed. Q1 2026 swung GAAP to -$12.6M loss (from +$1.9M); +16% Adjusted EBITDA only via three NEW add-backs ($16.6M pension buy-out + $11.2M servicing liability + $12.9M Greystone non-operating). Simultaneously DROPPED four non-GAAP comparables (Service Line Fee Revenue, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, Segment Operating Expenses, Fee-based Operating Expenses) — classic disclosure gating. Bermuda redomicile (11/27/25) installed shareholder-claim waiver and partial declassification delay to 2028. $66M payroll-tax claim + $52M reasonably possible additional loss are unreserved with imminent post-cutoff court ruling. Mitigants: debt management is genuinely strong (no covenant issues, $1.6B liquidity, 3.3x net leverage), revenue +9%, Adjusted EBITDA +13% FY25, AGM uncontested 97.7% Say-on-Pay support, no activists. Severity: 1 PASS / 5 MODERATE / 1 SEVERE / 1 RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE / 2 PASS (counting AGM and debt). Verdict: SHORT-tier with caveat — the insider-vs-narrative test fails decisively, the Greystone tail is structurally underdisclosed, and the simultaneous disclosure gating + GAAP swing is concerning. But operationally the core CRE services business is recovering (Capital Markets +19%, Leasing +8%) and the balance sheet is the strongest part of the story — so this is a softer SHORT than BL.
